about.role: Certified fitness coach (youth) | B.Ed in Physical Education | Tennis coach
about.bio:
I'm Shai — a physical education teacher (B.Ed), strength and performance coach, and tennis coach. Having grown up on the courts as a competitive tennis player and now coaching athletes across ages — from kids to national-league adults and national teams — I know firsthand the physical and mental demands of competitive sport.

My approach is demanding yet personal: no two sessions are the same, because no two sports are the same. Before loading the body, we map your sport's demands, your competition schedule, and your training history — including sensitivities, past injuries, and weak points that need reinforcement.

My goal is simple: build a stronger, faster, more resilient athlete who can produce explosive power and peak fitness all season long — without getting injured.
highlights: Smart load planning. Training built around your season and match schedule.
Sport-specific work. Speed, strength, and movement tailored to your sport.

items.title: Physiological recovery in competitive sport — the complete guide for coaches and athletes
items.excerpt: It's not just how hard you train, but how your body recovers between sessions. In this deep-dive (from my book on developing physical abilities) we explore hormonal regulation, training load, nutrition, sleep, and active recovery to reach peak performance.
items.body:
What is recovery and why it matters for performance
Think of training like a hammer breaking a wall. The session itself doesn't build you — it's the stimulus that creates controlled breakdown. Recovery is the rebuilding phase.
When we train at high intensity, the body undergoes immediate changes: depleted fuel stores, rising muscle acidity, and central nervous system fatigue. Recovery restores balance and can drive supercompensation — adaptation beyond your previous level.

Acute vs chronic recovery
Acute recovery happens in minutes to hours after training: heart rate drops, energy stores refill, and lactate is cleared. Chronic recovery spans days and weeks — muscle repair, aerobic adaptations, and hormonal balance.

Without adequate recovery, performance drops and injury risk rises. Recovery isn't separate from training — it's part of it.

faq.heading: Before you write — the answer might already be here
faq.subheading: These are the questions I hear most from athletes, parents, and coaches. Tap a question to open the answer.

items.question: From what age can strength training start?
items.answer: From about 12–13, with a base of coordination and motivation, structured supervised training can begin. Before that the focus is movement, play, and bodyweight work — not heavy loads. We always start with assessment and match load to age and sport.

items.question: Will strength training interfere with team practices?
items.answer: No — the goal is to complement what's missing in team training, not compete with it. The plan is built around your team schedule, emphasizing days with lower team load. When needed, we coordinate directly with your team coach.

items.question: How many sessions per week?
items.answer:
It depends on your plan and program.
Full online coaching is also available.

items.question: Where do sessions take place?
items.answer:
In-person sessions are in a gym or outdoor setup with sport-appropriate equipment.
Depends on the program.

items.question: Can I return after injury?
items.answer: Yes, after clearance from your physio. I don't replace medical treatment, but I take you from "cleared to return" to full competitive load — at a pace your body supports.

items.question: How do we start? What happens in the first session?
items.answer: Send a WhatsApp message or fill out the site form. We'll schedule a short call, then an intro session: basic movement screen, understanding your goals, and plan fit. No long commitment before we're sure it's the right match.

items.question: Is training adapted to my specific sport?
items.answer: Absolutely. Every plan is built personally for your sport's physical and movement demands (tennis, basketball, football, athletics, and more) — explosive power, change of direction, stability, and sport-specific injury prevention.

items.question: Does strength training hurt growth in young athletes?
items.answer: No — that's an outdated myth. Current sports science shows supervised resistance training with proper technique is safe for youth. It doesn't harm growth; it strengthens the musculoskeletal system, improves bone density, and reduces injury risk.

items.question: What if I have games, tournaments, or exams this week?
items.answer: Precise load management is a core part of my coaching. Plans are dynamic and adjust to your match schedule and physical/mental load. In heavy weeks we focus on recovery, strength maintenance, and prehab so you arrive fresh for competition.

items.question: How does follow-up work between sessions?
items.answer: Coaching doesn't end when the session ends. The process includes ongoing follow-up, weekly load adjustments, periodic testing, and continuous availability for questions and tweaks as needed.
